info.name: Kairox CMS
info.description: CMS (kx.cms): content reads for the website and the editors' admin API. Generated by scripts/gen_handoff.py from the code; read docs/handoff/CMS_API.md. Pick the Kairox local or staging environment. Sign in once (folder 01); the collection then renews the staff token by itself.

item.name: 01 Staff sign-in and MFA
item.description: Sign in with email + password, then a second step. First sign-in: email code, change the one-time password, enrol YOUR OWN authenticator app, then sign in again with the app.

request.description:
Step 1: email + password. Answers the second steps on offer (TOTP first; email code fallback).

**Who may call it:** public (no sign-in)

**Expected on success:** HTTP 200

exec: console.log(d.totp_enrolled ? "Next: 7. Second step with the authenticator code" : "Next: 2. Send the email sign-in code");

request.description:
Fallback second step: a 6-digit code to the staff member's work address (valid 10 minutes).

**Who may call it:** public (no sign-in)

**Expected on success:** HTTP 204

item.name: 3. Verify the email code (first sign-in / fallback)

request.description:
Step 2 with the email code: signed in with `mfa=false` (no approvals until TOTP is used).

**Who may call it:** public (no sign-in)

**Expected on success:** HTTP 200

exec: if (rc) { pm.environment.set("refresh_token", rc); }  // rotates on every renewal (auto-renew script)
pm.test("Signed in as " + d.user.role + " (mfa=" + d.mfa + ")", function () { pm.expect(d.access_token).to.be.a("string"); });
if (d.must_change_password) { console.warn("must_change_password=true: run '4. Change password' next"); }
if (!d.totp_enrolled) { console.warn("No authenticator yet: run '5. Enrol your authenticator app' next"); }

item.name: 4. Change password (first sign-in: replace the one-time password)

request.description:
Change the password (ends every other session).

**Who may call it:** any signed-in staff

**Expected on success:** HTTP 204

exec: console.log("Password changed. Copy new_password into staff_password in your environment, then run 1. Login again.");

item.name: 5. Enrol your authenticator app (shows a QR code)

request.description:
A new authenticator seed for the signed-in user (active only after /totp/confirm). Replacing an active authenticator needs a TOTP sign-in (D4) and the user is told by email.

**Who may call it:** any signed-in staff

**Expected on success:** HTTP 200

exec:
const tpl = `

Scan this QR code with your authenticator app
(Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, 1Password ...), or type the key by hand.
console.log("Open the Visualize tab of this response to scan the QR code. Then put the 6-digit code in totp_code and run 6.");

request.description:
The first code from the app switches TOTP on. Sign in again to get an MFA session.

**Who may call it:** any signed-in staff

**Expected on success:** HTTP 204

item.name: 7. Second step with the authenticator code (mfa=true)

request.description:
Step 2 with the authenticator app: `mfa=true` (needed for approvals, price edits, settings).

request.description:
End this session: the refresh token (cookie) and the session the access token names are revoked and the cookie cleared.

**Who may call it:** public (no sign-in)

**Expected on success:** HTTP 204

Recovery: a code to the work address. Always 202 (nobody learns which addresses exist); 429 when the rate limit for this IP or this typed address is reached (the same for unknown addresses, M3). L6: the code is mailed after the response, so a real address answers as fast as an unknown one.

**Who may call it:** public (no sign-in)

**Expected on success:** HTTP 202

Recovery step 2: the emailed code + a new password (min 12 characters); every session ends.

**Who may call it:** public (no sign-in)

**Expected on success:** HTTP 204

item.name: 15 CMS: website content and editors
item.description: D54: the website's content reads (public, cached) and the editors' draft / publish / versions / media API (content editor, admin, manager). Sign in first (folder 01).

request.description:
Site settings: company name, phones, emails, addresses, hours, social links, announcement bar, theme colours and fonts, the assistant's fixed texts, and whether product pages (PG-03) are live.

**Who may call it:** public (no sign-in)

**Expected on success:** HTTP 200

D55: the site map the AI assistant uses (pages and their section ids, families with their names and synonyms in six languages, products with their paths, factory-tour chapters). The website's instant navigation (layer 0) reads the same data.

**Who may call it:** public (no sign-in)

**Expected on success:** HTTP 200

One page with its section blocks (home, products, about, quality, clients, contact, privacy).

**Who may call it:** public (no sign-in)

**Expected on success:** HTTP 200

The product families, in their display order (HM-01, HM-04, PR-02).

**Who may call it:** public (no sign-in)

**Expected on success:** HTTP 200

The catalogue (PR-03), in catalogue order; filters as on the site: `family`, `q`, `range`.

**Who may call it:** public (no sign-in)

**Expected on success:** HTTP 200

PG-03: one product with its family, previous / next in the catalogue (PD-04) and up to four more from the same family (PD-05).

**Who may call it:** public (no sign-in)

**Expected on success:** HTTP 200

Any other collection, in display order: `tour_chapters` (HM-05), `stations` (QA-02), `faqs`, `certificates` (QA-04), `clients` (CL-02), `industries` (CL-01), `stories` (CL-03), `leadership` (AB-05, AB-06).

**Who may call it:** public (no sign-in)

**Expected on success:** HTTP 200

Every published page, family and product, in English and Arabic, for `/sitemap.xml` (§9).

**Who may call it:** public (no sign-in)

**Expected on success:** HTTP 200

Old-site addresses that move permanently to their new page (design doc §9): each product's `legacy_paths` (e.g. `/8325.php`) to its page (or its quick view until PG-03 is live).

**Who may call it:** public (no sign-in)

**Expected on success:** HTTP 200

Every content type with its JSON Schema (fields, types, limits), to draw the editor forms.

**Who may call it:** manager, md, admin, content_editor

**Expected on success:** HTTP 200

The documents of one content type, in display order, with their state (draft / published / changed = live with unpublished edits).

**Who may call it:** manager, md, admin, content_editor

**Expected on success:** HTTP 200

One document: its open draft (with `revision`, needed to save) and its live version.

**Who may call it:** manager, md, admin, content_editor

**Expected on success:** HTTP 200

Save the draft (creates the document when new). Send the `revision` you loaded; if a colleague saved meanwhile the answer is 409 and nothing is overwritten. Prices are refused (422 `cms_price`).

**Who may call it:** manager, md, admin, content_editor

**Expected on success:** HTTP 200

Put the draft live. The website re-renders the affected pages within about a minute; the AI's knowledge and the CRM product record follow automatically.

**Who may call it:** manager, md, admin, content_editor

**Expected on success:** HTTP 200

Take the document off the website (versions are kept; publish again to bring it back).

**Who may call it:** manager, md, admin, content_editor

**Expected on success:** HTTP 204

Throw the open draft away (a document that was never published disappears with it).

**Who may call it:** manager, md, admin, content_editor

**Expected on success:** HTTP 204

Every version, newest first (each publish is kept).

**Who may call it:** manager, md, admin, content_editor

**Expected on success:** HTTP 200

Copy an earlier version into the draft; publish it to go live again.

**Who may call it:** manager, md, admin, content_editor

**Expected on success:** HTTP 200

A 30-minute token that makes the website show drafts (Next.js draft mode).

**Who may call it:** manager, md, admin, content_editor

**Expected on success:** HTTP 200

exec: console.log("Add ?preview={{preview_token}} to a content read to see the drafts.");

request.description:
The library, newest first (`kind` = image, video, application (PDF) or model (3D)).

**Who may call it:** manager, md, admin, content_editor

**Expected on success:** HTTP 200

Step 1: ask where to upload. PUT the file to `upload_url` with `headers`, then confirm. Accepted: WebP, JPEG, PNG, AVIF, SVG (15 MB), MP4, WebM (300 MB), PDF (30 MB), GLB 3D models (50 MB).

**Who may call it:** manager, md, admin, content_editor

**Expected on success:** HTTP 201

exec: console.log("PUT the file to upload_url (Body > binary), then run Confirm.");
